facts.statement: Zhongjianornis was a beaked bird about the size of a pigeon that lived in China during the early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Zhongjianornis is a genus of beaked, pigeon-sized birds from the early Cretaceous period of China.

facts.statement: The only known fossil of Zhongjianornis was found at Jianchang in Liaoning Province within the Jiufotang Formation.
facts.quote: It is known from one fossil found at Jianchang, Liaoning Province, in rocks of the Jiufotang Formation, representing the type species Zhongjianornis yangi.

facts.statement: The species name Zhongjianornis yangi honors Yang Zhongjian, the founder of the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing, which holds the holotype.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen is in the collection of the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing, and the species Z. yangi is named for the IVPP's founder, Yang Zhongjian.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, catalogued as IVPP V15900, consists of a nearly complete skeleton missing only a few tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: This specimen is catalogued under the accession number IVPP V15900. It consists of a complete skeleton, possibly only missing a few tail vertebrae.

facts.statement: Zhongjianornis was formally described by Zhou, Zhang, and Li in a paper published in January 2010, which had been available online since 2009.
facts.quote: It was described by Zhou, Zhang and Li, in a paper published in January 2010 (though the paper had appeared on the Internet during 2009).

facts.statement: Zhongjianornis lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Zhongjianornis is classified within the superorder Dinosauria, order Saurischia, suborder Theropoda, and unranked family Avialae.
facts.quote: superordo: Dinosauria ordo: Saurischia subordo: Theropoda unranked_familia: Avialae

facts.statement: Initial analysis suggested Zhongjianornis was more primitive than Confuciusornis and lived before the evolutionary split between Euornithes and Enantiornithes.
facts.quote: They found that Zhongjianornis was more primitive than Confuciusornis, and that it predated the split between euornithean and enantiornithean birds.

facts.statement: Researchers noted that Zhongjianornis shared an expanded deltopectoral crest with basal birds like Jeholornis, suggesting it possessed an early flight architecture later replaced by a keeled breastbone.
facts.quote: The authors also reported that Zhongjianornis shared features with very basal birds like Jeholornis, Sapeornis and Confuciusornis, including a highly expanded deltopectoral crest, and suggest that this was an early flight architecture that was replaced by an enlarged, keeled breastbone in more advanced birds.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Zhongjianornis is a very primitive bird, as later analyses cast doubt on its basal position.
facts.quote: However, later analysis of the anatomy of Z. yangi cast doubt on this interpretation of the bird as very primitive.

facts.statement: A 2012 study argued that apparent primitive features in Zhongjianornis were due to poor bone preservation and that its anatomy is actually more similar to primitive Euornithes like Chaoyangia and Schizooura.
facts.quote: Research published in 2012 found that some of the apparently primitive features were due to poor preservation of the bones, and that Zhongjianornis is more similar in anatomy to primitive euornitheans like Chaoyangia and Schizooura.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis indicates that a very primitive position for Zhongjianornis in the bird family tree is unlikely given current evidence.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis showed that a very primitive position in the bird family tree for Z. yangi is unlikely given current evidence.
